results.evidence: db.migrate wraps a MigrationError from _apply and re-raises it with '; the database is now at version N' appended (cottonwood/db.py:253-256). _run_migrate prints 'error: ...' to stderr and returns EXIT_REFUSED (cottonwood/cli.py:82-84), and EXIT_REFUSED = 1 (cottonwood/cli.py:40). The new test builds 001_ok.sql (valid) and 002_bad.sql (invalid SQL) on a new db. It asserts main(['migrate']) == EXIT_REFUSED, that stderr contains '002_bad.sql' and 'version 1', and that PRAGMA user_version == 1. I ran it with `uv run --offline pytest -q tests/test_migrate_failure_reports_version.py -v`: 1 passed. The test redirects migrations by monkeypatching db.migrate, which is the same helper tests/test_migrate.py uses. It calls main() in-process, not a subprocess.
